Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaCore Inc. Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and using your microphone will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaCore Inc.'s second quarter results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. VitaCore Inc. delivered a solid second quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, and our outlook for the remainder of the year.  

I will now turn the call over to Mike Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Mike Chen:  
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $2.4 billion, representing a 5.2% increase on an organic basis compared to the prior year. Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 48.2%, driven by productivity savings, favorable pricing, and mix improvements from premium products. Operating income rose significantly, and diluted earnings per share came in at $0.92, with core EPS up 8%. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Let me now turn to our key strategic priorities and the meaningful progress we've made in the first half of the year, which are squarely driving our outperformance against the CPG industry backdrop. We delivered that 5.2% organic sales growth, with core EPS up 8%—well ahead of the sector's flat-to-low-single-digit growth amid persistent inflation and softening consumer sentiment in categories like snacks and household essentials.  

Our strategy remains anchored in four pillars: accelerated innovation, sustainability leadership, digital and omnichannel excellence, and supply chain resilience and cost discipline. These aren't just buzzwords; they're delivering tangible results, with contributions from these initiatives accounting for over 60% of our top-line growth and 40% of that gross margin expansion. Let me break it down pillar by pillar, with specific progress metrics, regional insights, and forward-looking commitments.  

First, on accelerated innovation: it's our growth engine, targeting high-velocity, high-margin categories like health and wellness, plant-based alternatives, and convenient formats—segments growing at 7-10% globally according to NielsenIQ data, outpacing the broader CPG market's 2-3%. We've launched 12 major SKUs in the first half, including our VitaBoost line of protein-fortified snack bars, which achieved 25% market share in the U.S. functional snacks category within three months, rivaling KIND and RXBAR velocities. New product sales hit $450 million, or 14% of total revenue—up from 10% last year—surpassing our 12% target. In beverages, our zero-sugar PureThirst sparkling water expanded to 15,000 U.S. doors via Kroger and Walmart partnerships, driving 18% household penetration lift and 12% average unit revenue uplift through premium pricing at $2.49 per unit. R&D investment rose 15% to $280 million, focusing on precision fermentation for dairy-free yogurts, with pilot success in Europe yielding 30% repeat purchase rates. Regionally, North America contributed 55% of innovation sales, fueled by health trends post-Ozempic demand shifts. In APAC, our Indonesia rollout of bite-sized NutriCrunch snacks captured 8% share in a $2 billion convenience pack market, growing 22% year-over-year. Looking ahead, we're on track for 16% new product contribution by year-end, with pipeline visibility into 2025 including CBD-infused wellness drinks pending regulatory nods.  

Second, sustainability leadership: this isn't a cost center—it's a competitive moat. With 72% of global consumers prioritizing eco-friendly brands per Kantar, we're leading with our Planet Positive 2030 roadmap: 100% recyclable packaging, 50% Scope 3 emissions cut, and regenerative agriculture across 40% of our supply base. Virgin plastic usage is down 42% year-over-year to 18% of total packaging, ahead of our 30% target—mirroring Unilever's progress but at lower cost through supplier switches to rPET from partners like Berry Global. Our sustainable cocoa initiative in West Africa sourced 65% Rainforest Alliance-certified beans for chocolate products, reducing water usage 28% per ton and supporting 15,000 farmer livelihoods. We launched aluminum-can EcoSip juices in Europe, boosting recyclability to 95% and driving 9% sales uplift in the UK via Tesco exclusives. Regionally, Europe—our second-largest market at 28% of sales—saw sustainability halo effects lift brand equity scores 15 points per YouGov, enabling 4% premium pricing power amid 3% category deflation. In LATAM, Brazil's palm oil traceability program mitigated 20% supply cost volatility from El Niño impacts. Financially, these efforts yielded $120 million in savings via circular economy efficiencies, flowing straight to the bottom line. We're committing an additional $150 million in CapEx for biomass energy at our top five plants, targeting 25% renewable energy by 2025.  

Third, digital and omnichannel excellence: e-commerce now represents 18% of CPG sales globally, up from 12% pre-pandemic per IRI, and we're outpacing at 22% of our revenue—targeting 30% by 2026. Our Shopper 360 platform integrates AI-driven personalization, DTC sites, and retailer apps. Online sales surged 32% to $1.2 billion, with Amazon velocity up 25% via sponsored ads and Subscribe & Save penetration at 35%. We launched AR try-on for personal care like shampoos and lotions on our app and Ulta.com partnership, lifting conversion 18% and basket size 22% to $45. Data analytics from 50 million loyalty members powered 15% targeted promo efficiency, reducing trade spend waste by $80 million. Regionally, China DTC via Tmall grew 45%, capturing urban millennials with KOL bundles—now 12% of APAC sales versus 7% industry average. In North America, club channels like Costco saw 10% comp growth from omnichannel bundling. Challenges persist in India, where quick-commerce volumes like Blinkit and Zepto rose 50% but margins compressed 200 basis points due to slotting fees; we're countering with private-label co-devs.  

Fourth, supply chain resilience and cost discipline: inflation eased to 2.5% in the first half, but input costs for cocoa up 35%, coffee up 20%, and ocean freight remain elevated. Our Agile Supply 2.0 program emphasizes nearshoring, AI forecasting, and zero-based productivity. Inventory turns improved to 8.2x from 7.1x, releasing $300 million in working capital. Procurement savings of 5% or $450 million via hedging 70% of 2024 commodity needs and vertical integration in spices with a new India facility. Service levels hit 98%, up from 92%, despite Red Sea disruptions—outperforming peers like Mondelez. Regionally, North America benefited from U.S.-Mexico nearshoring, cutting transit times 25%. APAC's Vietnam hub mitigated China tariffs, growing 15% ex-China. Gross margins expanded through $250 million in Project Horizon efficiencies—automation at 12 plants yielding 12% labor productivity gains.  

These priorities are interconnected: innovation fuels premiumization, now 45% of portfolio up 300 basis points year-over-year; sustainability unlocks retailer partnerships like Walmart's Regeneration aisles; digital amplifies reach; and supply chain protects margins. Collectively, they've driven 2.5 points of organic growth, 150 basis points of margin expansion, and ROIC above 18%. Risks include consumer downtrading in a 3.1% U.S. unemployment environment and APAC regulatory hurdles for fortified foods. But with $2.5 billion in dry powder, we're poised for bolt-on M&A—like our $400 million acquisition of a European plant-based dairy startup—to accelerate. In summary, we're executing at high velocity, positioning VitaCore for sustained 4-6% organic growth and 10%+ core EPS CAGR through the cycle.  

Now, turning to our capital expenditure plans and priorities, which remain a cornerstone of our strategy to drive sustainable growth, enhance operational resilience, and deliver superior returns on invested capital—or ROIC—in the dynamic CPG landscape. Our industry faces persistent headwinds from inflation in raw materials like cocoa, palm oil, and PET resins, alongside softening consumer demand in non-essential categories amid economic uncertainty. Yet, we're leaning into these challenges with a disciplined $1.2 billion capex program for fiscal 2024, representing a 12% increase year-over-year from $1.07 billion in 2023. This guidance assumes a mid-single-digit U.S. GDP growth trajectory and stable FX rates, with flexibility to adjust down by up to 10% if consumer spending weakens further, as we've seen in recent NielsenIQ data showing a 2.1% category decline in North American households.  

Our capex allocation is strategically weighted toward three pillars: supply chain modernization at 45% or $540 million, sustainability and efficiency initiatives at 30% or $360 million, and innovation and digital transformation at 25% or $300 million. This mix is designed to boost our free cash flow conversion to over 95% of adjusted EBITDA by 2026, while targeting a blended ROIC uplift of 150 basis points to 14.5% over the next three years.  

First, supply chain modernization—our largest bucket. We're prioritizing capacity expansion and automation to address labor shortages and rising wage pressures, which have driven CPG manufacturing costs up 8-10% globally per recent McKinsey reports. In North America, accounting for 40% of our capex or $480 million total regionally, we're investing $250 million in a greenfield facility in the U.S. Southeast—specifically Georgia—to ramp up production of our high-margin protein snacks and plant-based beverages, akin to Beyond Meat's supply chain pivot but scaled for our OmniFit brand. This site will feature Industry 4.0 robotics from partners like ABB, targeting 25% labor productivity gains and reducing downtime by 30% through predictive maintenance AI. Capacity utilization across our NA network currently sits at 82%, and this addition will push it toward 90% by Q4 2025. In EMEA, $200 million with €120 million toward debottlenecking plants in Poland and the Netherlands for household care products like our EcoShield detergents, responding to EU regulatory pressures on water usage and aligning with Unilever's sustainability playbook—expecting 15% throughput increase via high-speed filling lines from Krones. APAC gets $150 million, focused on Indonesia and India for personal care expansion; for instance, an $80 million aseptic packaging line for our NutriGlow yogurt drinks to capture the booming $50 billion Indian dairy market, growing at 12% CAGR per Statista. Latin America rounds out at $110 million, emphasizing resilient sourcing for coffee and snacks amid El Niño volatility—think a $50 million upgrade to our Brazilian roasting facility with blockchain traceability, mirroring Starbucks' tech investments.  

Second, sustainability and efficiency at $360 million, underscoring our commitment to net-zero by 2040, ahead of peers like P&G's target. We're targeting a 20% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions intensity by 2026. Key initiatives include $150 million in energy retrofits: solar microgrids and heat pumps at 15 plants globally, yielding 18% energy cost savings based on our pilot in Mexico. In packaging, $100 million funds recycled content scaling—e.g., 50% post-consumer resin in our Refresh beverage bottles, similar to Coca-Cola's PlantBottle evolution, which should cut virgin PET usage by 30,000 tons annually. Water stewardship gets $60 million, including precision irrigation tech for sugarcane sourcing in Brazil via partnerships with The Climate Corporation, addressing 25% yield volatility we've seen in recent seasons. Regionally, EMEA leads at 40% of this bucket due to stringent PFAS bans, while APAC focuses on wastewater recycling to comply with China's dual-carbon goals.  

Third, innovation and digital transformation at $300 million is about future-proofing the top line. R&D capex hits $120 million, fueling 15 new SKUs launches in 2024—think functional beverages with adaptogens for our Revive energy line and zero-sugar variants for OmniFit to counter Ozempic-driven appetite suppression trends impacting 5-7% of snack volumes per IRI data. We're also building a $100 million Center of Excellence in Chicago for AI-driven consumer insights, integrating Salesforce Einstein and Nielsen data lakes to accelerate time-to-market from 18 to 12 months. On the digital front, $80 million enhances end-to-end supply chain visibility with SAP S/4HANA and IoT sensors, aiming for 99.9% on-time delivery—critical as retailer OTIF penalties from Walmart and Tesco average 2-5% of sales. This includes warehouse automation with autonomous mobile robots from Locus Robotics, targeting 25% fulfillment cost reductions in our DTC e-commerce hubs. We've seen e-commerce CPG sales grow 22% year-over-year to 18% of total per Kantar, so we're prioritizing last-mile EV fleets: $40 million for 500 electric vans in urban NA and EU markets, partnering with Rivian, with projected 30% logistics savings by 2026.  

Strategically, these investments are gated by rigorous NPV hurdles—minimum 15% IRR—and phased returns: 40% in Year 1 from efficiency gains, 60% in Years 2-3 from volume and margin expansion. We're maintaining capex at 4-5% of sales long-term, below the industry average of 5.5% per Deloitte, to preserve our A- credit profile. Risks include commodity spikes—e.g., cocoa at $10,000 per ton—and permitting delays, but our $300 million capex reserve provides a buffer. This $1.2 billion plan positions us to outpace CPG peers like Colgate and Kellogg in ROIC expansion, while navigating a fragmented retail environment—from Amazon's dominance to discounters like Aldi gaining 200 basis points share. We're confident it'll support 5-7% organic growth and 100+ basis points margin accretion.  

Next, let's dive into our advertising and promotion, or A&P, investments, which remain a cornerstone of our growth strategy in this dynamic CPG landscape. A&P is not just a line item—it's our engine for driving household penetration, velocity, and market share in categories like household care, snacks, and beverages, where we're up against fierce competition from the likes of Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and PepsiCo.  

For the second quarter, our global A&P spend totaled $285 million, representing 11.8% of net sales—up 8 basis points year-over-year from 11.7%. This moderation from our elevated 12.5% in Q1 reflects disciplined reallocation amid softer category growth, influenced by persistent inflation and downtrading in value segments. Year-to-date, we're at $820 million, or 12.1% of sales, in line with our full-year guidance of 11.8-12.2%. Importantly, this spend is delivering strong returns: our blended ROI across all channels hit 2.7x, a 14% improvement from 2.4x last year, and ahead of our long-term target of 2.5x+. We're measuring this rigorously through our proprietary Marketing Mix Modeling platform, enhanced with Nielsen and Kantar data, which attributes incremental sales lift while controlling for baselines, pricing, and distribution.  

Breaking it down by channel, we've continued our strategic pivot to high-efficiency media. Traditional TV and out-of-home advertising, 25% of spend at $71 million, saw ROI of 1.8x—solid for upper-funnel brand building on icons like our FreshGlow laundry detergent, but down slightly due to linear TV fragmentation. Trade promotions, at 35% or $100 million, delivered 3.2x ROI, bolstered by shopper marketing precision: we optimized head-on displays and feature pricing with Kroger and Albertsons, driving a 6% lift in ACV distribution for SnackJoy chips amid private label pressure.  

The real story is digital and retail media networks—now 40% of total A&P at $114 million, up from 32% last year. Here, ROI soared to 4.1x, fueled by our technical initiatives. We've rolled out an AI-powered demand-side platform in partnership with The Trade Desk, leveraging first-party data from our loyalty apps and CRM systems to target high-LTV households with 25% greater precision than third-party cookies. For instance, on Amazon Advertising and Walmart Connect—which together captured 60% of our retail media budget—we achieved 5.2x ROI on sponsored products for our Quench beverages, converting 18% of impressions to sales during Prime Day. This is incrementality-tested via geo-holdout experiments, showing a true 12% sales uplift net of halo effects.  

Regionally, performance varied but trended positive. In North America, our largest market at 55% of spend or $157 million, ROI was 2.9x—driven by digital's dominance amid e-commerce's 15% category penetration. We leaned into connected TV on platforms like Roku and Hulu, where FreshGlow's Stain Fighter campaign generated 150 million impressions and a 22% awareness lift per YouGov tracking. Europe, at 25% of spend or $71 million, faced headwinds from regulatory scrutiny on HFSS advertising, capping ROI at 2.3x; however, our localized promo efficiency in the UK with Tesco's Clubcard data yielded 3.5x on SnackJoy, offsetting a 4% year-over-year spend cut. Emerging markets—Latin America and APAC—punched above their 20% spend weight at $57 million with 3.4x ROI, thanks to hyper-local tactics: in Brazil, JioMart partnerships drove 28% volume growth for Quench, while in India, quick-commerce tie-ups with Blinkit delivered sub-ROAS 4x during festive gifting.  

Strategically, post-iOS privacy changes and the cookieless future, we've invested $15 million year-to-date in clean room tech with Google's Privacy Sandbox and our own zero-party data lake, which has improved targeting match rates by 30%. We're also piloting always-on performance marketing with machine learning for dynamic budget shifting—shifting 10% of underperforming TV dollars to TikTok Shop in real-time, where Gen Z trials for SnackJoy variants are converting at 8%. Looking ahead, we expect Q3 A&P at 12.0% of sales, with ROI expanding to 2.8x+ as holiday activations ramp: think Black Friday retail media blitzes and Super Bowl adjacency for FreshGlow. Our A&P discipline is yielding tangible results—contributing 40% to our organic sales growth—while positioning us for sustained share gains in a market where peers like Mondelez are signaling similar digital shifts. We're balancing short-term ROI with long-term equity.  

Turning to performance by our key categories and brands, we delivered balanced growth across the portfolio. Net sales were $2.4 billion, up 5% as reported and 3% organically at constant currency. Adjusted EPS was $0.85, beating guidance, driven by disciplined pricing, supply chain efficiencies, and strong category execution. Gross margins expanded 210 basis points to 42.8%, reflecting 3-4% price/mix actions and productivity savings from our $150 million zero-based budgeting program. We gained or held share in 85% of measured markets, with velocity up 2 points on average.  

Beverages, our largest at 28% of sales generating $1.18 billion, grew 4% organically. Volume was flat, but pricing and premium mix drove upside—sparkling waters and functional beverages over legacy carbonated soft drinks. Flagship AquaPure grew 7%, capturing 1.2 share points in North America to 22% overall, fueled by AquaPure+ Immunity vitamin-infused still water with 25% ACV distribution gains and 15% household penetration lift in 90 days. This aligns with premiumization where consumers trade up 8-10% in price tiers amid health shifts. North America +6% organic from e-commerce velocity up 18% via Amazon and Walmart+; EMEA +3% despite softer on-premise; APAC -2% from China lockdowns, countered by low-sugar green tea variants. We're investing $50 million in sustainable packaging—100% recycled PET for AquaPure by year-end—to tap 60% of millennials prioritizing eco-credentials per Kantar.  

Snacks & Confectionery, 22% of sales at $920 million, accelerated to +6% organic, outpacing IRI's +2%. CrunchyBites savory snacks surged 12%, gaining 0.8 share points to 18% in U.S. retail from air-fried protein crisps resonating with keto/low-carb—trial rates 22% in test markets. Confectionery +2%, pressured by 30% YTD cocoa inflation, but value-engineered gum held margins. LATAM +9% with CrunchyBites tortilla chips expanding via 5,000 new JBP points with Soriana and Chedraui; North America +5%, tempered by private label; EMEA navigating HFSS by reformulating 40% portfolio to <5g sugar per serving. Our Snack Smart DTC platform at 1.5 million subscribers boosts direct margins 500 basis points with first-party data for bundling.  

Personal Care, $850 million or 20% of sales, grew 3% organically, skincare +8% offsetting softer oral care. GlowEssence exploded 15%, adding 1.5 share points to 14% in prestige via hyaluronic acid serum—#2 in U.S. multi-door per SPINS—riding skinification with 45% seeking actives like retinol. APAC +7% with K-beauty dupes on Shopee/Flipkart GMV +25%; North America +2% with prestige pivot via Sephora lifting ASPs 6%. $100 million R&D in microbiome tech launches probiotic shampoos next quarter for $15 billion scalp health TAM.  

Home Care, 18% at $760 million, +2% organic amid deflation. Fabric care +3% via concentrated formulas reducing dosage 30%; SparkleClean gained 0.5 share points to 16% in North America from viral TikTok #SparkleCleanChallenge with 50 million views and 12% sales lift. EMEA flat from energy crisis, mitigated by app subscriptions retaining 75%; LATAM +4% on multipacks. Resilience hubs in Vietnam/Poland cut lead times 20%.  

Health & Wellness, 12% at $500 million, surged 9%—double category rate per Euromonitor. VitalBoost vitamins/probiotics +14%, +2 share points to 11% in natural channels as immune demand up 20% search volume. Collagen shots hit $50 million run-rate. North America +10%, APAC +12% via Alibaba. AI app personalization shows 30% repeat uplift. Category diversification de-risks against inflation now trending to 4%. On track for 4-5% full-year organic.  

On geographic performance, our balanced portfolio across developed and emerging markets delivered resilient results. Total net sales grew 6% reported to around $12.8 billion equivalent pace, organic 5%, with pricing 4 points, volumes 2 points, offset by 1-point FX. Sales mix 58% developed, 42% emerging.  

Developed markets delivered 2.5% organic at $7.4 billion, North America 32% of sales +3.2% from share gains in health/wellness; UltraClean Pods mid-teens volume, +1.2 share in U.S. fabric care per Nielsen with bio-based enzymes. E-commerce 28% of sales +400 bps via Amazon and UniCore Direct app at 15 million users. Europe 20% flat 0.8% from inflation/energy; Dove Regenerative Serum +1.5 mix in premium. €150 million localized hubs in Poland/Spain mitigate Red Sea. Australia/Japan 1-2% from CrunchWave vending. Margins +120 bps to 22.1% from $500 million ERP project 85% complete.  

Emerging markets surged 12.4% to $5.4 billion. APAC ex-Japan 22% +15%; China +14.2% beauty/baby, Youth Elixir +2.1 share; India +22% foods/homecare Ariel +1.5 points sachets; SE Asia +12% instant noodles. LATAM 12% +9.8% despite FX; Brazil beverages +11% coolers, Mexico snacks +8%. Africa/ME/Vietnam +13% from $200 million distribution adding 300,000 POS. Margins -50 bps to 18.2% from mix/inflation, limited by pricing/hedges. Strategy: defend premiumize developed, invest emerging with $800 million FY24 capex like India facility, Seller Hub app 2 million downloads. Developed 2-4% FY24, emerging 10-14%; natural hedge 65% local sourcing.  

Finally, our outlook for organic sales growth into Q3 and FY25. Q3 5.2% ahead guided, 2.8% volume/mix, 2.4% pricing—strongest core volume since pre-pandemic. 14 billion-dollar brands drove 65% top-line. Guiding 3-5% organic Q3, FY25 4-6%. Pricing 1.5-2.5% tapering, mix 0.5-1% from premium like organic Pringles, probiotic yogurts +12% penetration. Volume 1.5-3% from Velocity 2.0 AI planograms +200 bps ACV; Q3 launches plant-based Tide pod, Gatorade chews for $15B functional. North America 55% 4-6% grocery/mass Walmart/Kroger +4%; EMEA 20% 2-4% beauty +8%; APAC 15% 3-5% Olay/Pringles; LATAM 10% flat-2% pricing room. CPG 2025 plan $500M: digital 25% sales Subscribe&Save 18%; nearshoring $200M; wellness 10 launches. Share +80 bps ex-soap/cleaning. Risks unemployment >4.2%, commodities +20% hedged 70%. Positions for 2-3% industry, 7-9% EPS.  

Next, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.  

Lisa Patel:  
Thank you, Mike. We saw strong performance in our core brands, particularly AquaPure and GlowEssence. Our digital marketing efforts are driving significant engagement, and we are seeing strong results from our Shopper 360 campaign, which ties directly into the high ROI we've discussed, with AR features and personalized targeting lifting conversions across channels.  

Following me, Raj Singh will provide an update on our supply chain initiatives.  

Raj Singh:  
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs. We are implementing new technologies and processes like Agile Supply 2.0 and Project Horizon automation to enhance responsiveness to changing market conditions. We are also actively working to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions through nearshoring and AI forecasting, achieving those 98% service levels and inventory improvements Mike highlighted.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. Instructions for participating in the question-and-answer session will be provided. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan.  

John Smith:  
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in emerging markets?  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thanks, John. As Mike detailed, emerging markets were our high-growth engine at 12.4% organic, more than twice developed markets. APAC ex-Japan led with 15%, China rebounding 14.2% on premium beauty like Youth Elixir gaining 2.1 share points, and our rural DTC via Alibaba reaching 500 million consumers with distribution to 1.2 million outlets up 18%. India exploded 22% on 10% volume in foods and homecare, Ariel sachets for low-income households tapping 300 million new consumers per McKinsey. LATAM 9.8% despite FX, Brazil beverages 11% via 50,000 coolers. We're investing heavily, like the $300 million Tamil Nadu facility and Seller Hub app, sustaining 10-14% growth with 65% local sourcing hedge.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Goldman Sachs.  

Emily Davis:  
How are you managing inventory levels given the current economic uncertainty?  

Mike Chen:  
Great question, Emily. Inventory turns improved to 8.2x from 7.1x, releasing $300 million working capital through AI forecasting and zero-based productivity in Agile Supply 2.0. We're nearshoring like U.S.-Mexico cutting transit 25%, Vietnam hub for APAC, and hedging 70% commodities. Service at 98% despite disruptions, with capex in automation and robotics ensuring flexibility if uncertainty persists—we have buffers in our $1.2 billion plan.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Morgan Stanley.  

Tom Wilson:  
Can you discuss the progress on your sustainability goals and any related cost implications?  

Raj Singh:  
Absolutely, Tom. Sustainability is embedded core, with Planet Positive 2030 on track: virgin plastic down 42% to 18%, sustainable cocoa 65% certified saving water 28% per ton, EcoSip 95% recyclable +9% sales. $120 million savings from circular efficiencies, $360 million capex in solar/heat pumps yielding 18% energy savings, recycled PET cutting 30,000 tons virgin, precision irrigation for Brazil sugarcane. Committing $150 million biomass for 25% renewables by 2025—net positive to margins, enabling premium pricing like 4% in Europe, and ROIC uplift.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Anna Lee with Barclays.  

Anna Lee:  
What are your expectations for pricing elasticity in the coming quarters?  

Lisa Patel:  
Thanks, Anna. Pricing contributed 2.4% this quarter, expecting 1.5-2.5% in Q3 tapering but surgical—3-5% on commodity SKUs like cleaners/snack bars, flat on premium wellness to protect velocity. Elasticity strong in emerging like India/Brazil 4% room, premiumization mix +0.5-1% from organics/probiotics. A&P ROI 2.7x supports, with digital 4.1x funding targeted promos. FY25 4-6% organic embeds this discipline.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions. We remain committed to delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the VitaCore Inc. Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Performance by key categories and brands
Geographic performance: developed vs. emerging markets
Organic sales growth guidance for next quarter/year

aspect_summary.Key strategic priorities and progress: VitaCore's strategy anchored in four pillars: accelerated innovation (12 SKUs launched, $450M new product sales at 14% of revenue), sustainability leadership (virgin plastic down 42%, $120M savings), digital/omnichannel excellence (e-com 22% of revenue, +32% growth), supply chain resilience (inventory turns 8.2x, $450M procurement savings); drove 5.2% organic sales growth, 8% core EPS rise.
aspect_summary.Capital expenditure plans and priorities: $1.2B FY2024 capex (up 12% YoY), allocated 45% ($540M) supply chain modernization (NA greenfield facility, EMEA debottlenecking), 30% ($360M) sustainability/efficiency (energy retrofits, recycled packaging), 25% ($300M) innovation/digital (R&D, AI center); targets ROIC +150bps to 14.5%, FCF >95% EBITDA by 2026.
aspect_summary.A&P (advertising & promotion) spend and: Q2 A&P $285M (11.8% sales), YTD 12.1%, FY guide 11.8-12.2%; blended ROI 2.7x (+14% YoY), digital/retail media 4.1x (40% of spend); contributed 40% to organic growth, strong in emerging markets at 3.4x ROI.
aspect_summary.Performance by key categories and brands: Q2 organic +3%: Beverages (28%) +4% (AquaPure +7%), Snacks/Confectionery (22%) +6% (CrunchyBites +12%), Personal Care (20%) +3% (GlowEssence +15%), Home Care (18%) +2% (SparkleClean share gains), Health & Wellness (12%) +9% (VitalBoost +14%); share gains in 85% markets.
aspect_summary.Geographic performance: developed vs. em: Developed (58% sales) +2.5% organic (NA +3.2%, Europe +0.8%); emerging (42%) +12.4% (APAC ex-JP +15%, India +22%, LATAM +9.8%); emerging as high-growth engine with heavy investment.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth guidance for next q: Q3 3-5% organic (pricing 1.5-2.5%, volume/mix 1.5-3%); FY25 4-6%; long-term 4-6% organic, 10%+ core EPS CAGR; regional: NA 4-6%, EMEA 2-4%, APAC 3-5%, LATAM flat-2%.
